title: Make the test task reproducible
summary: Declare the test gem, wire a Rake test task, and diagnose a local command that bypasses Bundler.

objectives.description: Declare a test dependency and a Rake task.
Find a command that ignores the bundle.
Explain why bundle exec changes dependency resolution.

hints: The Gemfile names gems; Bundler resolves and locks versions.
A Rake test task loads a test library and a file pattern.
t.libs adds the test directory to the load path.
task default: :test makes the test task the default.

misconceptions.description: Relying on a globally installed test gem.
misconceptions.feedback: A global gem ignores the project's lockfile. bundle exec runs the versions Bundler resolved.

misconceptions.description: Leaving the default task as a placeholder.
misconceptions.testDescription: The Rakefile defines a test task over test/**/*_test.rb.
misconceptions.feedback: A default task that only prints a message reports success without running tests. Define a real Rake::TestTask.

misconceptions.description: Assuming rake and bundle exec rake are equivalent.
misconceptions.feedback: bundle exec constrains the load path to the bundle's locked gems. Plain rake may load a different installed version.

misconceptions.description: Installing a test gem without a version constraint.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Declaring gem "minitest" with no version so CI can resolve a different release than development.
misconceptions.feedback: A version constraint plus Gemfile.lock keeps local and CI runs on the same release.

sections.title: The Gemfile is the dependency contract
sections.body: A Gemfile starts with source "https://rubygems.org" and lists gems such as gem "minitest", "~> 5.25". bundle install resolves versions and writes Gemfile.lock. Commit the lockfile so CI installs the same graph. bundle exec then runs a command with exactly those gems on the load path.

sections.title: Rake names the work
sections.body: require "rake/testtask" loads the test task helper. Rake::TestTask.new(:test) do |t| ... end configures a task: t.libs << "test" adds the test directory, and t.pattern selects test/**/*_test.rb. task default: :test makes a bare rake run the suite.

sections.title: Reproduce the CI command
sections.body: If CI runs bundle exec rake test, run the same command locally. ruby -Itest test/inventory_test.rb bypasses Bundler and can load another installed minitest. For a one-off file, bundle exec ruby -Itest test/inventory_test.rb keeps the bundle. The lockfile is the evidence that both environments agree.

steps.title: Local pass, CI fail
steps.prompt: CI uses a different minitest release than the developer machine. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
hints: The local command starts with ruby directly.
A direct ruby command can see globally installed gems.
Use bundle exec for the local run too.

fixes.label: Run bundle exec rake test locally as well.
Delete Gemfile.lock so both machines resolve fresh.

steps.explanation: bundle exec restricts the load path to the locked bundle. Running ruby directly can load a globally installed minitest, so the two environments test different code.

hints: Bundler controls which gem versions are visible.
rake alone uses the ambient Ruby environment.
